q: Which of the following buildings held the title of tallest building in the world when it was completed in 1931 and held it for nearly 40 years?
n: The Empire State Building (Shreve, Lamb & Harmon), completed in 1931, was the world's tallest building until the World Trade Center's North Tower topped it in 1970. Source: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH), Tallest Buildings history.

q: Which building, known for its striking black and gold facade symbolizing “black gold" (petroleum), was an ambitious early Art Deco tower in Los Angeles, but only a portion of its design was realized due to the Great Depression?
n: The Richfield Tower in Los Angeles (Morgan, Walls & Clements, 1929) had a black and gold Art Deco facade symbolizing "black gold". The Depression cut the planned complex short, and the tower was demolished in 1969. Source: Los Angeles Conservancy; Gebhard & Winter, Architecture in Los Angeles.

q: Which skyscraper famously secured the title of tallest building in the world—if only briefly—by secretly assembling a 125-foot spire inside its tower and raising it in a surprise move that shocked the architectural world?
n: William Van Alen's Chrysler Building (1930) secretly assembled its 125-ft stainless-steel spire inside the crown. Hoisting it into place made it briefly the world's tallest building. Source: CTBUH; Stern et al., New York 1930.

q: Which building complex in New York, anchored by a 70-storey tower, is known for its integration of multiple skyscrapers, public plazas and art installations, and was a major urban project developed during the Great Depression?
n: Rockefeller Center is a multi-building Art Deco complex built during the Depression, centered around 30 Rockefeller Plaza, a 70-story skyscraper. It became a model for urban planning by combining offices, retail, public art, and open space in one integrated development. Rockefeller Center is a Depression-era complex of 14 original Art Deco buildings anchored by the 70-storey 30 Rockefeller Plaza. It integrates plazas and public art. Source: Stern et al., New York 1930; National Historic Landmark nomination.

q: Which skyscraper features decorative elements modeled after car parts, such as hubcaps and radiator caps, reflecting the identity of its automotive sponsor?
n: The Chrysler Building, designed by William Van Alen, was commissioned by the head of the Chrysler Corporation. Its ornamentation includes eagle gargoyles resembling hood ornaments and hubcap-style friezes, making it a rare example of corporate branding embedded in Art Deco architecture. The Chrysler Building's ornaments are modeled on Chrysler cars: hubcaps, radiator caps and winged hood ornaments in the form of eagle gargoyles. Source: Stern et al., New York 1930; NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report.

q: Republic Act No. 1378 in the Philippines primarily governs the design, installation, maintenance, and regulation of which of the following systems?
o: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems
n: Republic Act No. 1378, also known as the Plumbing Law of the Philippines, sets the standards and regulations for the design, installation, maintenance, and regulation of water supply and drainage systems in buildings. The law ensures public health and safety by setting professional practices for plumbers. RA 1378, the National Plumbing Code, regulates the design, installation and maintenance of plumbing systems: water supply, drainage, venting and sanitary works. Source: RA 1378 (1955) and the Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (1999).

q: Republic Act No. 9514 in the Philippines primarily governs the safety measures, regulations, and standards for which of the following systems in buildings?
o: Prevention, suppression, and protection from hazards
n: Republic Act No. 9514, known as the Fire Code of the Philippines, regulates the prevention, suppression, and protection from fire hazards in buildings and establishments. It mandates safety protocols, fire prevention measures, and the installation of firefighting equipment to ensure public safety. RA 9514, the Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008, governs fire prevention, suppression and protection from fire hazards in buildings and facilities. Source: RA 9514, Sec. 2–3, and its 2019 RIRR.

q: What is the smallest stair width allowed by the Fire Code of the Philippines for an occupant load of less than 50?
n: The Fire Code requires exit stairs to be at least 1,120 mm wide, or 915 mm where the total occupant load served is less than 50. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Means of Egress – Stairs, Table of minimum widths).

q: Percentage of allocated fire reserve over average daily demand supply in an elevated tank.
n: Per the exam key, the fire reserve in an elevated tank is taken as 20% over the average daily demand. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Water Supply – Storage Tanks) and RA 9514 RIRR (fire water reserve).

q: Who approves and signs an attachment plan?
n: Per the exam key, an attachment plan for electrical service connection is prepared, signed and sealed by a Professional Electrical Engineer. Source: RA 7920 (New Electrical Engineering Law), Sec. 2 and 31; Philippine Electrical Code Part 1.

q: Which of the following best describes the use of color in ancient Greek temple architecture?
o: Bold and vibrant colors like red, blue, and gold were applied to architectural details such as friezes and pediments
Pure white marble was left unpainted to emphasize structural form and clarity
Neutral grays and blacks were used to enhance the contrast with natural light
Subdued earth tones were used to reflect the simplicity and humility of the gods
n: Archaeology and paint traces show Greek temples were polychrome. Friezes, pediments and moldings were painted in strong reds, blues and gilding, not left as bare white marble. Source: Brinkmann, Gods in Color; Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture (Greece).

q: What color, when used extensively in commercial interiors, has been shown to suppress appetite and is therefore rarely used in restaurants?
n: Blue is the color least associated with food. Studies of color and appetite find it suppresses appetite, so it is rarely used for restaurant interiors. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response; Spence & Piqueras-Fiszman, The Perfect Meal.

q: Which movement in architectural history emphasized pure primary colors, black, white, and gray as essential to spatial harmony and visual order?
n: Among the choices, the Bauhaus (and the related De Stijl movement) championed pure primaries with black, white and gray as the basis of visual order. Source: Droste, Bauhaus 1919–1933; Curtis, Modern Architecture Since 1900.

q: An architect is designing a vibrant co-working space intended to boost creativity and maintain visual harmony. She selects a color scheme using three hues spaced equally around the color wheel—such as red, yellow, and blue. What type of color scheme is she applying?
n: A triadic scheme uses three hues equally spaced (120° apart) on the color wheel, such as red, yellow and blue. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color Schemes); Itten, The Art of Color.

q: What are the four core colors of traditional Islamic architecture?
n: Traditional Islamic architecture favors green (paradise), blue (heavens, in tilework), gold (divine light, in calligraphy) and white (purity). Source: Blair & Bloom, The Art and Architecture of Islam; Hillenbrand, Islamic Architecture.

q: What is the lowest recommended professional fee for an architect acting as the project manager?
n: The recommended fee for an architect acting as project manager is 2% to 5% of the project cost, so the lowest is 2%. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 9 (Project/Construction Management Services).

q: Article 3 of the Code of Conduct defines the relations of the architect and the
n: Per the exam key, in the architect's code of ethical conduct, the article after duties to the public sets out the architect's relations with the client. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 200 (Code of Ethical Conduct); RA 9266 IRR (Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility).

q: Minimum fine of an architect violating the Code of Conduct.
n: Per the exam key, violations of the law and its code of conduct carry a minimum fine of ₱100,000, with imprisonment as the court decides. Source: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004), Sec. 45 (Penal Provisions).

q: Percentage of performance bond
n: Per the exam key, the performance bond is commonly set at 15% of the contract price in private construction contracts. Note: under RA 9184 for government projects it is 5% to 30% depending on the form of security. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions – Bonds); RA 9184 Revised IRR, Sec. 39.

q: Percentage of guarantee bond
n: A guarantee bond in the form of a surety bond is set at 30% of the contract price. Cash or bank guarantees are lower, at 5–10%. Source: RA 9184 Revised IRR, Sec. 39 (Performance Security); UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions – Bonds).

q: An architectural firm is hired to design a veterinary hospital along Commonwealth Ave., Quezon City. The firm offered an all-in design package for the project, which has a total project cost of ₱35 million. What is the recommended professional fee to be collected by the firm?
n: The all-in design package means the DAEDS, and since the veterinary hospital is a Group 3 project under the Regular Design Services, the RPF is 7% of the PPC. 7% of 35 million is 2.45 million. A veterinary hospital is Group 3. An all-in package (architecture plus engineering) is DAEDS, at 7% for PCC of ₱50 million and below: 7% × ₱35,000,000 = ₱2,450,000. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.3 (Group 3).

q: Upon signing of the service agreement, an owner is required to pay the 5% acceptance fee to the architect. From which cost is the acceptance fee computed?
n: Since at this stage of a regular design service, no design and specifications are produced, the ideal basis for the acceptance fee is a ballpark estimate using floor area and the unit cost per area. The acceptance fee (5% of the fee) is paid on signing, before any estimate exists. It is computed from the estimated project cost: floor area × unit construction cost. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Manner of Payment – Upon signing of the agreement.

q: Which architect benefits the most in a value-pricing method of compensation?
n: Per the exam key, value pricing ties the fee to the value created for the client. In this reviewer's framing it benefits most the building administrator managing the asset. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 4.2 (Value-based Pricing).

q: An architect specializing in architectural lighting submitted his final design to the client. He received the corresponding fee for the work. How much is the remaining fee to be collected by the architect?
n: Lighting design follows the AI/acoustics/lighting payment schedule: 30% on the preliminary design and 50% on the final design. The remaining 20% is paid during construction. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.2 (Manner of Payment).

q: Which of the following is the first deliverable of an architect hired for the physical plan of a sports complex?
n: FRDP means Framework Development Plan (FRDP). For physical planning of large sites such as a sports complex, the first deliverable is the Framework Development Plan (FRDP). The detailed and master development plans follow. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.2 (Physical Planning Services – deliverables).

q: Which of the following dictums is associated with Louis Sullivan?
o: “It is the pervading law of all things organic and inorganic, of all things physical and metaphysical, of all things human and all things superhuman, of all true manifestations of the head, of the heart, of the soul, that the life is recognizable in its expression, that form ever follows function. This is the law.”
“In all my works, light is an important controlling factor.”
“I think white is the most wonderful color of all, because within it one can find every color of the rainbow.”
“Creative work is expressed in our time as a union of technology and humanity.”
n: Take note that this long paragraph is the exact wordings of Louis Sullivan in his book "The Tall Office Building Artistically Considered" (1896). Louis Sullivan wrote that "form ever follows function" in "The Tall Office Building Artistically Considered" (1896). Source: Sullivan, Lippincott's Magazine (1896).

q: Which of the following dictums is associated with Kenzo Tange?
o: “I think white is the most wonderful color of all, because within it one can find every color of the rainbow.”
“Creative work is expressed in our time as a union of technology and humanity.”
“In all my works, light is an important controlling factor.”

“It is the pervading law of all things organic and inorganic, of all things physical and metaphysical, of all things human and all things superhuman, of all true manifestations of the head, of the heart, of the soul, that the life is recognizable in its expression, that form ever follows function. This is the law.”
n: Kenzo Tange described creative work in our time as a union of technology and humanity. Source: Tange, Pritzker Prize acceptance and writings (1987); The Pritzker Architecture Prize archive.

q: Which of the following dictums is associated with Richard Meier?
o: “Creative work is expressed in our time as a union of technology and humanity.”

“It is the pervading law of all things organic and inorganic, of all things physical and metaphysical, of all things human and all things superhuman, of all true manifestations of the head, of the heart, of the soul, that the life is recognizable in its expression, that form ever follows function. This is the law.”
“I don't believe architecture has to speak too much. It should remain silent and let nature in the guise of sunlight and wind.”
“The responsibility of an architect is to create a sense of order, a sense of place, a sense of relationship.”
n: Richard Meier described the architect's responsibility as creating a sense of order, place and relationship. He is also known for his praise of white. Source: Richard Meier & Partners, interviews and Pritzker Prize (1984) materials.

q: Which of the following dictums is associated with Tadao Ando?
o: “I think white is the most wonderful color of all, because within it one can find every color of the rainbow.”
“Creative work is expressed in our time as a union of technology and humanity.”
“In all my works, light is an important controlling factor.”

“It is the pervading law of all things organic and inorganic, of all things physical and metaphysical, of all things human and all things superhuman, of all true manifestations of the head, of the heart, of the soul, that the life is recognizable in its expression, that form ever follows function. This is the law.”
n: Tadao Ando stated that light is an important controlling factor in all his works, as in the Church of the Light. Source: Ando, Pritzker Prize acceptance (1995); Frampton, Tadao Ando.

q: Which of the following dictums is associated with Rem Koolhaas?
o: “The mother art is architecture. Without an architecture of our own we have no soul of our own civilization.”
“Architecture is a dangerous mix of power and impotence.”
“A house is a machine for living in.”
n: "Architecture is a dangerous mix of power and impotence" is Rem Koolhaas's line from S,M,L,XL (1995). The other quotes are by Wright, Le Corbusier and Mies. Source: Koolhaas & Mau, S,M,L,XL.

q: An architect designs a museum building with a striking central dome, surrounded by lower, curved gallery spaces. The dome acts as a focal point, while the galleries appear secondary in importance. Which design principle is demonstrated here?
n: The central dome, being larger and more prominent, establishes a visual hierarchy, guiding visitors’ attention and emphasizing its importance. Hierarchy makes one element dominant by its size, shape or position, like a central dome, while the surrounding galleries read as secondary. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Ordering Principles – Hierarchy).

q: A new residential building features vertical fins on the facade, creating a rhythmic pattern that makes the structure appear taller and more dynamic. Which design principle is primarily applied in this context?
n: Repeated vertical fins create rhythm, a regular recurrence of elements, and their verticality makes the facade look taller and more dynamic. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Rhythm and Repetition).

q: In a civic center, the architect uses a massive stone-clad tower at the entrance and gradually reduces the height and volume of the adjacent buildings. This creates a sense of progression and importance leading to the main building. What design principle is exemplified?
n: By graduating the size from the large tower to smaller buildings, the architect uses scale to create a sense of prominence and approach. Grading size from a massive tower down to smaller buildings uses scale to give the main building prominence and a sense of approach. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Proportion and Scale; Hierarchy).

q: A library is designed with open, interconnected reading spaces that flow seamlessly from one area to another. The architect uses similar materials and colors throughout to maintain visual continuity. Which design principle does this illustrate?
n: Using the same materials and colors throughout, with flowing connected spaces, produces unity: the parts read as one coherent whole. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Unity and Variety).

q: An office building has a highly reflective glass facade, contrasting with the adjacent brick-clad residential block. The architect intended to highlight the difference between the modern workspace and the traditional homes. Which design principle is primarily demonstrated?
n: Setting a reflective glass facade against traditional brick deliberately sharpens the difference between them. That is the principle of contrast. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Which of the following is considered a cult-type structure in Egyptian architecture?
n: The Luxor Temple is a cult-type structure because it was built for the worship of gods, particularly the Theban god Amun. Unlike pyramids, mastabas, and rock-hewn tombs—which are mortuary structures for the dead—the Luxor Temple was used for religious rituals and festivals. Egyptian cult temples housed the daily worship of a god's statue, as at Luxor Temple (Amun). Pyramids, mastabas and rock-cut tombs were funerary. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt); Arnold, The Encyclopedia of Ancient Egyptian Architecture.

q: Which of the following is considered a mortuary structure in Egyptian architecture?
n: Although Karnak and Luxor technically refers to a region, in the context of the question, they may refer to the temple complexes. Among the options, only Tomb of Hatshepsut is the only mortuary strucutre, others are cult temples. The Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari was built for the queen's funerary cult. Karnak, Luxor and the Temple of Horus at Edfu are cult temples. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture; Arnold, The Encyclopedia of Ancient Egyptian Architecture.

q: Which of the following is primarily considered a mortuary structure designed to house the deceased in early Egyptian architecture?
n: The mastaba was a flat-roofed, rectangular tomb with sloping sides used in early Egyptian dynasties for elite burials. The mastaba, a flat-topped rectangular mud-brick or stone tomb over a burial shaft, was the main tomb of early dynastic Egypt. Pyramids grew out of it. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt); Lehner, The Complete Pyramids.

q: Which of the following, symbolizing Lower Egypt and often associated with fertility and creation, is a common motif in Egyptian column capitals?
n: The papyrus was the emblem of Lower Egypt (the Delta). It appears in bundled and open-flower (campaniform) column capitals. Source: Arnold, The Encyclopedia of Ancient Egyptian Architecture (Columns); Fletcher, A History of Architecture.

q: Which of the following, symbolizing Upper Egypt and also representing rebirth and purity, is frequently depicted in temple decorations?
n: The lotus was the emblem of Upper Egypt and a symbol of rebirth and creation. It is common in capitals and temple reliefs. Source: Arnold, The Encyclopedia of Ancient Egyptian Architecture; Wilkinson, Reading Egyptian Art.

q: A Filipino architect is building a KPO agency offering regular architectural design services to overseas clients. Which SPP Document can be used to regulate their service rates?
n: SPP Document 202 specifically mentioned that it does not cover BPO and KPO companies offering architectural services to overseas clients. The SPP documents on regular design services do not cover BPO or KPO firms that offer architectural services to overseas clients, so none of the listed documents regulates their rates. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Scope of Application; UAP SPP Doc. 202.

q: An architect is engaged in a regular design service for a 162-sqm, 3-storey single-detached residence in an exclusive subdivision in Quezon City. The client hired separate engineers and construction supervisors to implement the architect's design. The development cost reached ₱10,140,000, with 88.76% allocated to construction cost. How much is the professional fee for the architect?
n: This is a tricky question. Remember that the 6.0% RPF for Residential DADS contract is computed from PCC or Project Construction Cost. Take note the difference of development cost and construction cost (refer to SPP Document 202). Therefore: e PCC =P10,140,000 x 88.76% = P9,000,264 e RPF = P9,000,264 x 6.0% = P540,016. A single-detached residence is Group 4. With separate engineers the service is DADS, at 6% of PCC. PCC = 88.76% × ₱10,140,000 = ₱9,000,264, so the fee = 6% × ₱9,000,264 = ₱540,016. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4).

q: In the previous item, if the architect hired the other allied professionals so the client does not need to, what is the professional fee?
n: This is now a DAEDS contract so the RPF is 10% of PCC. Therefore, P9,000,264 x 10% = P900,026.4. If the architect hires the allied engineers, the service becomes DAEDS: 10% for Group 4. Fee = 10% × ₱9,000,264 = ₱900,026. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4 – DAEDS 10%).

q: The client loves the design and decides to hire the architect again for the very same design on another lot within the same subdivision. What should be the professional fee for the 2nd project?
n: When a design is re-used without changes, the fee for the second building is 50% of the RPF. It is 40% for the third, and 30% for the fourth and later buildings. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.7 (Repetitive Construction).

q: The client loves the design of the building and decided to hire again the architect for the very same design on another lot within the same subdivision. What should be the professional fee for the 2nd project?
n: A design reused without changes on another lot is charged 50% of the original fee for the second building. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.7 (Repetitive Construction).

q: What is required for a project to be exempted from certain provisions of the zoning ordinance?
n: A Certificate of Exception (COE) can be obtained through a city or municipal council resolution. The councilors of a city/district/municipality will deny or approve the application for COE, in consultation with the zoning authority and OBO. Take note that barangay councilors (kagawads) are also involved in the decision making for a project. An exception to zoning provisions (a certificate of exception or variance) is granted through a resolution of the city or municipal council, on the zoning board's recommendation. Source: HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance (Exceptions and Variances); Local Government Code (RA 7160), Sec. 447/458.

q: Which of the following is not typically included under construction preliminaries?
o: Site fencing and temporary access roads
n: Structural concrete and reinforcement bars are permanent materials used in the actual construction of the building’s structure. In contrast, preliminaries refer to temporary works and administrative requirements—such as site setup, permits, and temporary utilities—that support the project but aren't part of the final building. Construction preliminaries (general requirements) cover site establishment: fencing, temporary roads, site office, utilities, permits and insurance. Structural concrete and rebars are permanent work items. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions); Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (General Requirements).

q: An architect specializing in acoustics is hired to design the sound quality and control for a school auditorium. The total cost of the acoustic works is ₱800,000. Which of the following is an acceptable professional fee for the project?
n: According to SPP Document 203 Specialized Architectural Services, the range of Recommended Professional Fee for Acoustic Design is 10-15% of the cost of works. Therefore, only P96,000 is within the range (12% of P800,000). Acoustic design is paid at 10% to 15% of the cost of work: ₱80,000 to ₱120,000 for ₱800,000 of works. Only ₱96,000 (12%) falls in that range. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.1.1.

q: What type of professional service is offered when an architect provides BIM modeling and consultancy to convert conventional building designs into BIM-based systems?
n: BIM modeling and consultancy are specialized architectural services, offered beyond regular design services and requiring special expertise. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Specialized Architectural Services (SPP Doc. 204).

q: In the previous scenario, which of the following methods of compensation is least ideal?
n: BIM conversion is substantial, ongoing work, best paid by fixed fee or time-based methods (MDPE, salary cost times a multiplier). An honorarium is a token payment for one-time appearances and is the least suitable. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.2.1 (Methods of Compensation).
